description: The three layers, ingestion, storage, transformation, caches, protection, governance and sharing; Gen1 credit figures. Checked November 2026.

cards.front: Snowflake's three layers: {{c1::cloud services}}, {{c2::compute (warehouses)}} and storage.
Which layer holds the result cache and the query optimizer?
When are cloud-services credits actually billed?
cards.back: Only the part above 10% of that day's warehouse credits

cards.front: How is a warehouse billed when it resumes?
cards.back: Per second, with a 60-second minimum each time it starts

cards.front: Gen1 credits per hour for X-Small, Small, Medium, Large, X-Large?
Gen2 X-Small credits per hour on AWS?
How do you keep a new warehouse on Gen1 where Gen2 is the default?
Which column of SHOW WAREHOUSES tells Gen1 from Gen2?
A Medium finishes in 1 minute; an X-Small takes 4. Which costs more?
cards.back: Neither: 4 credits/h × 1 min equals 1 credit/h × 4 min

cards.front: Many users queue on one warehouse. Scale up or out?
How long does Snowflake keep load metadata that stops COPY INTO reloading a file?
What does FORCE = TRUE on COPY INTO risk?
cards.back: Loading files again, so duplicate rows

cards.front: What does CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE do to COPY load metadata?
cards.back: Wipes it, so the next COPY reloads every file still in the stage

cards.front: How is Snowpipe billed since December 2025?
cards.back: 0.0037 credits per GB ingested, no per-file charge

cards.front: Snowpipe bills a gzipped CSV at which size?
Snowpipe auto-ingest on AWS: S3 event → {{c1::SQS}} → Snowpipe.
Which object holds IAM trust to a bucket so nobody puts keys in a stage?
Which table type stores data as Apache Iceberg in your own bucket?
Micro-partition size, and measured how?
Why does an UPDATE create Time Travel history?
cards.back: Micro-partitions are immutable, so new ones are written

cards.front: What lets Snowflake skip micro-partitions during a query?
Does SELECT from a stream advance its offset?
cards.back: No; only DML that consumes the stream does

cards.front: How does a task skip runs when there's no new data?
What does TARGET_LAG = '10 minutes' mean?
cards.back: Data at most ~10 minutes stale (a target), not a refresh every 10 minutes

cards.front: What TARGET_LAG should intermediate dynamic tables use?
Result cache lifetime?
cards.back: 24 hours, renewed on reuse up to 31 days from the first run

cards.front: Name two things that stop result cache reuse.
cards.back: Changed underlying data; a different query text or a function like CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()

cards.front: What happens to the warehouse cache on suspend?
Which session parameter turns result reuse off for benchmarking?
Which feature speeds point lookups on high-cardinality columns?
Can a materialized view join two tables?
What caps Query Acceleration Service spend?
Maximum Time Travel on Standard Edition?
Maximum Time Travel on Enterprise for permanent tables?
Fail-safe period, and for which tables?
Who can recover data from Fail-safe?
Why make ETL work tables transient?
cards.back: No Fail-safe storage for data you can rebuild

cards.front: Restore a table to just before a bad DELETE.
Does cloning a single table copy its grants?
cards.back: No, unless you add COPY GRANTS

cards.front: Which pipes are skipped when a database is cloned?
cards.back: Pipes that read from internal stages

cards.front: Who pays for compute used in a reader account?
In a direct share, who pays for the queries?
cards.back: The consumer, on its own warehouses

cards.front: Why share secure views rather than plain views?
cards.back: Consumers can't see a secure view's definition

cards.front: Name four Enterprise-only governance policies.
Which system role should create everyday objects?
cards.back: SYSADMIN (or custom roles granted to it)
